root_idea.summary: The root centers on a covering or sheath that encloses and protects something.
root_idea.development: This covering principle extends to botanical envelopes, a sleeve or head-covering, and the derived state of being covered or concealed. The Quranic plural أَكْمَام refers to such botanical coverings.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic plural is normalized to the singular dictionary citation form كِمٌّ.

senses.definition: A covering or sheath enclosing a fruit, flower, or date-palm inflorescence.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic form occurs as the plural أَكْمَام and refers to the enclosing coverings of date palms and their fruit or flowers; translations such as “coverings” and “sheaths” reflect this context.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An interrogative word asking “how many?” or, by extension, “how much?” and “how long?” when an amount or period is understood.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may also occur in a declarative construction indicating a large number; the noun used to specify the quantity varies in grammatical case according to the construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The sleeve of a shirt, the part that covers the hand or arm.
A cap or rounded skullcap covering the head.
A quantity or amount, especially as an answer to “how many?”
The cancamum tree, a named botanical tree.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Pointer to synonymous entries; it supplies no independent definition.

cautions: The Quranic group أَكْمَام is normalized to the plant-covering noun كِمٌّ; the separately attested homographic interrogative كَمْ is retained as a distinct Classical Arabic entry.
